statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail is 21%, inside the watch band and below the 25% block threshold, while Stress stays high at 71%.
recommendation: Tail remains below the block threshold, so the deterministic mapping stays at WATCH for NQ futures and NAS100 CFD alike. A 30-year yield at 5.64%, its highest since 2002, crude near $90 and an unresolved Strait of Hormuz negotiation keep Stress high without establishing an observed one-way Nasdaq-100 price path. The narrowest window of raised conditional risk is the 1 October cluster between 12:00 and 15:00 UTC, covering jobless claims, the US cash open and ISM Manufacturing.
headline: Nasdaq-100 closes at its session low while futures hold mid-range; Tail stays in the watch band
body: The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed at 30,408.50, up 0.23%, but finished exactly at its session low after trading as high as 30,630.45. NQ futures last printed 30,725.75, up 0.37%, roughly in the middle of a 30,512.25 to 30,905.50 range, and are now inside the daily CME halt between 21:00 and 22:00 UTC. That combination, a weak cash close against futures that recovered more than 200 points from their own low, is a genuinely two-sided tape rather than a persistent one-way path, and VIX at 16.34 confirms no volatility stress. Breadth was rotational rather than uniformly weak: the Dow fell 0.86% to 50,906.05 and the S&P 500 slipped 0.25% to 7,651.54 while the Nasdaq Composite rose 0.24%, with Alphabet up about 3%. September closed with the Dow down 4.9% and the Nasdaq up 1.7%. The dominant stress channel is rates: the 30-year yield rose to 5.64%, its highest level since 2002, and the 10-year reached 5.29%, with the 2-year at 4.89% on the latest H.15 release. WTI crude at $90.34 and an unresolved seven-day Strait of Hormuz proposal, to which Iran has received Washington's response through Qatari mediators, sustain an energy and geopolitical risk premium. Offsetting that, August PCE at 3.4% against 3.7% expected pared October Federal Reserve hike odds to 37% from more than 70% a week earlier, and Micron reported record fiscal Q4 revenue of $54.23 billion with first-quarter guidance of $61.5 billion plus or minus $1.5 billion after the close. Those are Stress and Confidence inputs; none of them is observed evidence of mean-reversion failure, so Tail stays at 21%. Shared Finviz context was not usable for this run because the published file is about 22 hours old and marked partial, so this assessment rests entirely on independent primary-source research.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly slots carry a published Claude assessment. Tail sat at 15-18% through the Asian and European hours, then stepped into the watch band from 12:00 UTC as the US session developed, peaking at 23% between 15:00 and 16:00 UTC and easing to 21-22% into the cash close. Stress held between 65% and 72% throughout, and the dominant mode was mixed for all but the first three slots.
outlookSummary: The path holds in the watch band with three slots easing to the low band during the orderly mid-Asia hours between 02:00 and 04:00 UTC. Conditional Tail rises again from 11:00 UTC and peaks at 23% across 13:00-15:00 UTC, where jobless claims, the US cash open and ISM Manufacturing stack inside three hours; those slots are scored as event/whipsaw because a two-sided reaction is the base case and a sustained directional leg would be the first genuine amplifier. Tail then decays through the US afternoon, ticking up once for the 19:00 UTC power hour before the cash close. Stress stays between 68% and 73% throughout on long-end yields and crude, and Confidence drifts from 87% to 84% as the projection extends from the verified evening reference levels.
